utility.notes: SCE's own 'Incorporated Cities and Counties Served by SCE' fact sheet (updated 3/17/2025) explicitly lists 'Pico Rivera' by name among the cities in its service area. PRIME's own site also confirms: 'PRIME purchases power on behalf of its customers while Southern California Edison (SCE) delivers it.'

value.name: PRIME (Pico Rivera Innovative Municipal Energy)
value.notes: PRIME is the City of Pico Rivera's own Community Choice Aggregation (CCA) program (not Clean Power Alliance), confirmed directly via its own official site (poweredbyprime.org/about): 'the locally run, not-for-profit, public energy service created by the City of Pico Rivera.' Primary service tiers are 'PRIME Power' (50% renewable) and 'PRIME Future' (100% renewable); the site does not explicitly name a single default among them. Opt-out to direct SCE service is available.

county.notes: Pico Rivera is a well-documented Los Angeles County city; also listed under Los Angeles County in SCE's own service-area fact sheet.

value.name: SGIP - Residential Solar and Storage Equity
value.administrator: Southern California Edison (SCE), under the CPUC's Self-Generation Incentive Program
value.description: Storage incentive of $1,100/kWh paired with a solar incentive of $3,100/kW, funded via a $280 million CPUC-authorized budget that opened for reservations June 2, 2025. Administered by SCE across its entire distribution territory, which includes Pico Rivera/Los Angeles County.
value.eligibility: PG&E or SCE residential customers (general market tier)

battery_programs.notes: Same statewide CPUC-administered SGIP program already confirmed for other SCE-territory records this session, reused as a utility-level fact.

value.name: SolarAPP+ Approval Document with inspection checklist
Solar contractor name and contractor license number
Site Plan (location of major components on the property)
Electrical Diagram (PV/ESS configuration, wiring, overcurrent protection, inverter, disconnects, required signs, AC connection)
Specification sheets and installation details for all manufactured components (PV modules, inverters, combiner box, disconnects, mounting system)
Signed Solar Affidavit (must be completed before the inspection date)

required_documents.notes: Per the City's own Residential Solar Permit Checklist (updated 1/16/2025).

value: Schedule an inspection by logging into the SolarAPP+ account or the Pico Rivera website, finding the permit number, and requesting an inspection
Requests should be made at least 24 hours in advance; specific dates/times requested are not guaranteed
One inspection covers PV system, electrical, structural, and fire safety compliance; typically completed within 1 day of the appointment

value.notes: The City's own Residential Solar Permit Checklist states 'Residential permits processed through Solar APP+ are typically processed within 2 to 3 days' (not guaranteed). Residential installations with battery storage, or systems that don't qualify for SolarAPP+, are typically processed within 2 to 4 business weeks instead.

value.program_or_pathway: SolarAPP+ (systems under 10 kW, no battery) / standard Building Division submission (over 10 kW or with battery storage)
other_conditions: Residential systems exceeding 10 kW, or those including battery storage, must be submitted directly to the Building Division rather than through SolarAPP+
Contractors must hold both a valid City of Pico Rivera Business License and a C-10 Electrical Contractor License
Permits expire 1 year after issuance if work has not started
